  C. RESOLUTION NO. 23-59 APPROVING A REQUEST FOR TEMPORARY
  STREET CLOSURE ON THE 800 BLOCK OF COMMERCIAL AVENUE

  The Public Works Department received a request from Jason De La Torre, owner
  of the property located at 864 Commercial Avenue, for a temporary street
  closure. The purpose of this request is to hold a block party for Ogopogo
  Brewing’s 5th Anniversary Celebration. The block party will be held on Saturday,
  October 21, 2023, on the 800 block of Commercial Avenue from 4:00 p.m. to
  9:00 p.m. There is no fiscal impact to the budget for this event.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 23-59 authorizing
  closure on the 800 block of Commercial Avenue from South Gladys Avenue to
  the end of the cul-de-sac from 4:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. on Saturday, October 21,
  2023.

  D. AWARD OF CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT NO. 23-04 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $216,200 PLUS A 10% CONTINGENCY TO PALP, INCORPORATED, DBA
  EXCEL PAVING COMPANY FOR THE REHABILITATION OF A STORM DRAIN
  LINE LOCATED ON SAINT ALBANS ROAD

  A section of the storm drain system located on Saint Albans Road between the
  existing maintenance manhole at Coolidge Drive and a catch basin located at
  Roses Road needs replacement due to substantial decay of the existing
  corrugated steel pipe. The deteriorated pipe has led to several sinkholes in the
  street and will likely continue to occur if the decay is not addressed. Palp,
  Incorporated, dba Excel Paving Company, is the lowest responsive bidder for
  the rehabilitation of a storm drain line located on Saint Albans Road. Funding
  for the project will be from Measure W funds in the amount of $216,200, plus
  a 10% contingency of $21,620.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 3, 2023  3
   California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve plans and specifications for the Saint Albans Road Strom Drain
  Rehabilitation Project;
  2. Award the contract to Palp, Inc., dba Excel Paving Company; and
  3. Authorize the City Manager to execute Construction Contract No. 23-04 and
  approve a purchase order in the amount of $237,820 which includes a 10%
  construction contingency.

  E. PROFESSIONAL  SERVICES  AGREEMENT  WITH  ARCHITECTURAL
  RESOURCES GROUP FOR THE HISTORIC RESOURCES SURVEY PHASE 2 IN
  THE AMOUNT OF $39,995

  On April 5, 2022, the City Council approved a Professional Services Agreement
  with Architectural Resources Group (ARG) for the preparation of a citywide
  historic resources survey. ARG has completed the Citywide Historic Resources
  Survey Report Phase 1. A new agreement with ARG is required, to move forward
  to Phase 2 of the survey. If approved, as part of Phase 2 of the project, ARG will
  continue with outreach and education work with the community, and further
  evaluate and document properties that may qualify to be on the City’s inventory
  and be designated as a local historic individual resource, resource contributing
  to a district, and potential historic district(s). Funding for Phase 2 has been
  approved as part of the Fiscal Year 2023-24 budget in the Community
  Development Department Contractual Services Account No. 121-810-14-22-
  000.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the Professional Services
  Agreement with Architectural Resources Group for Phase 2 of the Historic
  Survey and authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement and issue a
  purchase order in the amount of $39,995.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – October 3, 2023  4
  6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

 7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. FUND BALANCE RESERVE POLICY AMENDMENT AND ESTABLISHING
  RESERVE BALANCES FOR FISCAL YEAR 2022-2023

  A key component of a well-managed organization is a written policy that
  provides for prudent fund balance reserve levels. The City’s fund balance reserve
  policy was established in May 2019 and has been amended multiple times. The
  proposed amendment to the policy refines the City’s contingency reserve levels
  as well as adding a commitment of fund balance option to set funds aside for
  capital replacement and the retiree healthcare liability. Additionally, this report
  recommends reserve levels for Fiscal Year 2022-23, which is currently under
  audit. Contingency reserves of 25% will be established in the general fund as
  well as committing funds for capital replacement and Other Post-Employment
  Benefits (OPEB) funding for Fiscal Year ended June 30, 2023.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt the following resolutions:

  1.  Resolution No. 23-61 Amending the Fund Balance Reserve Policy; and
  2.  Resolution No. 23-62 Establishing Unassigned General Fund Contingency
  Reserves and Committing Fund Balance in the General Fund.

  B. ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 23-63 APPROVING THE CITYWIDE
  HISTORIC RESOURCES SURVEY REPORT

  A citywide historic resource survey is a list of potentially-eligible cultural
  resources throughout a city. A historic resource survey provides the basis for an
  inventory of cultural resources. On September 13, 2023, the Historic Preservation
  and Cultural Resource Commission adopted a resolution recommending the City
  Council to approve the Citywide Historic Resources Survey Report. There is no
  fiscal impact related to this item.

  This project is exempt from the requirements of the California Environmental
  Quality Act (CEQA), pursuant to Sections 15061(B)(3) and 15262 of the CEQA
  Guidelines. This includes a section known as the general rule and exempts

   projects where it can be seen with certainty that there is no possibility that the
  activity in question may have a significant effect on the environment.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 23-63 approving
  the Citywide Historic Resources Survey Report.

  C. COMMUNITY SPECIAL EVENTS 2023-24

  Community engagement events or special events are held throughout the year.
  During the Budget Study Session and at times during the year, the subject of
  community special events has come up. The City Council has raised ideas about
  new or enhanced events. Staff is bringing this item for further discussion and
  Council direction.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council discuss the upcoming events for the
  remainder of 2023 and 2024 and provide direction to staff.

MINUTES OF OCTOBER 3, 2023
  REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

I  CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Harrington called the regular meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at
  6:31 P.M. on Tuesday, October 3, 2023, in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South
  Mission Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Council Member Chan .

  ROLL CALL

  Council Members Present:  Eric Chan, Tony Ding, Denise Menchaca, Vice Mayor
  John Wu, and Mayor John R. Harrington.
  Council Members Absent:  None.
  Staff Members Present:  Public Works Director/City Engineer Greg de Vinck, City
  Attorney Keith Lemieux, Community Services Director

I  Rebecca Perez, Chief City Clerk Sharon Clark, Human
  Resources/Risk Management Director Edward Macias,
  Finance Director William Kaholokula, Community
  Development Director Aldo Cervantes, Police Chief
  Edward Elizalde, Fire Division Chief Newton Ong, and
  Assistant City Clerk Marilyn Bonus.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS

  Chief City Clerk Clark provided information for the public on how to view the meeting and
  how to request meeting agendas.

  1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  Hearing no objection, Mayor Harrington announced that the Agenda Order was
  approved.
  2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. INTRODUCTION OF POLICE OFFICER TUSHAR GULIANI

I  Pol ice Chief Elizalde made the presentation.

  B. SAN GABRIEL VALLEY MOSQUITO & VECTOR CONTROL DISTRICT UPDATE

  Clerk of the Board Jerry Mireles made the presentation.

  3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING M INUTES  Page 1 of 6  October 3, 2023
   George Valdez, resident, provided comments questioning various points of
  consideration for City membership with the San Gabriel Chamber of Commerce.

  And rew, resident, questioned various City expenditures and the City's financial
  position relative to a potential bond measure for a public safety facility, and requested
  that the meeting be adjourned in memory of Senator Feinstein .

  Chasity Jennings-Nunez, resident and Human Equity, Access and Relations (HEAR)
  Commission Chair, reported on the Commission's 2nd Annual Mental Wellness Expo,

I  recognized the City of Hope for its donation to the event, acknowledged dignitaries
  who attended, and thanked those who worked on the event.

  Sonia Martin stated her concerns about the San Gabriel Chamber of Commerce, asked
  the City Council to request an audit of the Chamber's finances, and submitted a
  document for the record .

  Neil T. Torrance, resident, spoke in opposition to the Tentative Tract Map for 1975 and
  1985 S. Del Mar Avenue and submitted a petition against the project.

  4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  A motion was made by Council Member Menchaca, seconded by Council Member
  Chan, to approve Consent Calendar Items 4A - 4E as presented .

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  CHAN, DING, MENCHACA, WU, HARRINGTON
  NOES:  NONE

I  ABSTAIN:
  ABSENT:
  NONE
  NONE

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The City Council approved :

  1. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of September 19, 2023.
  2. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of September 19, 2023.

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The City Council approved September 7, 2023, and September 15, 2023, Registers
  of Demands and Warrants for the payment of City expenditures.

  C. RESOLUTION NO. 23-59 APPROVING A REQUEST FOR TEMPORARY STREET
  CLOSURE ON THE 800 BLOCK OF COMMERCIAL AVENUE

I  The City Council adopted Resolution No. 23-59 authorizing closure of the 800
  block of Commercial Avenue from South Gladys Avenue to the end of the cul-de-
  sac from 4:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. on Saturday, October 21, 2023.

  D. AWARD OF CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT NO. 23-04 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $216,200 PLUS A 10% CONTINGENCY TO PALP, INCORPORATED, DBA EXCEL
  PAVING COMPANY FOR THE REHABILITATION OF A STORM DRAIN LINE
  LOCATED ON SAINT ALBANS ROAD

  The City Council :

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 2 of 6  October 3, 2023
   1. Approved plans and specifications for the Saint Albans Road Strom Drain
  Rehabilitation Project;
  2. Awarded the contract to Palp, Inc., dba Excel Paving Company; and
  3. Authorized the City Manager to execute Construction Contract No. 23 -04 and
  approved a purchase order in the amount of $237,820 which includes a 10%
  construction contingency.

  E. PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH ARCHITECTURAL RESOURCES

I  GROUP FOR THE HISTORIC RESOURCES SURVEY PHASE 2 IN THE AMOUNT
  OF $39,995

  The City Council approved the Professional Services Agreement with Architectural
  Resources Group for Phase 2 of the Historic Survey and authorized the City
  Manager to execute the agreement and issued a purchase order in the amount of
  $39,995.

  5. PUBLIC HEARING - NONE

  6. CONTINUED BUSINESS- NONE

  7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. FUND BALANCE RESERVE POLICY AMENDMENT AND  ESTABLISHING
  RESERVE BALANCES FOR FISCAL VEAR 2022-2023

  Finance Director Kaholokula made the presentation.

I  Clarifying discussion included that money in the fund balance reserve is being
  actively invested, and details of the capital replacement fund and Other Post-
  Employment Benefits (OPEB) reserves.

  There was no public comment.

  Discussion included that the capital replacement fund and OPEB reserves will be
  memorialized as separate items; the current unrestricted reserve level is 29%; 25%
  reserve as the ideal level; preference to transfer more to OPEB liabilities; overage
  from the 25% reserve will go half to capital replacement and half to OPEB liabilities,
  but be still part of the general fund and available; for Fiscal Year 2023-24, $250,000
  will go to the OPEB Trust which earns higher interest; keeping money in the general
  fund puts the City in a better position for a bond rating; maintaining a 25% reserve
  provides stability in case of an economic downturn; the main driver of OPEB liability
  increases are the increases in health costs and new retirees; and as of January 1,
  2022, new hires are not being added to the liability except for the employer's
  portion of Medicare.

I  A motion was made by Council Member Menchaca, seconded by Council Member
  Chan, to adopt:

  1. Resolution No. 23-61 Amending the Fund Balance Reserve Policy; and
  2. Resolution No. 23-62 Establishing Unassigned General Fund Contingency
  Reserves and Committing Fund Balance in the General Fund.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  CHAN, DING, MENCHACA, WU, HARRINGTON
  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 3 of 6  October 3, 2023
   NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN :  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  B. ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 23-63 APPROVING THE CITYWIDE HISTORIC
  RESOURCES SURVEY REPORT

  Planning Manager Samantha Tewasart and Consultant Andrew Goodrich of
  Architectural Resources Group (ARG) made the presentation .

I  Clarifying discussion included that the San Gabriel Mission, the Mission Playhouse,
  and other properties are already designated as Historic; potential historic district
  versus a planning district area that has special character but generally lacks the
  integrity for listing as a historic district; the purpose of this repo rt to inform the
  Historic Preservation and Cultural Resource Comm ission (HPCRC) who propose
  properties to be designated; and pros and cons of historical designation for
  property owners.

  Senya Lubisich, resident and HPCRC Chair, commended the report and process
  during which the HPCRC had many opportunities to give feedback; expressed
  appreciation that non-parcel items were included; and commented on economic
  benefits of investing in historic character.

  Andrew, resident, questioned the purpose of the survey. Mayor Harrington
  responded that it is a foundational document that sets up mechanisms to fac ilitate
  decision-making by commissions to preserve the character of the City.

  Discussion included benefits of the survey; acknowledgment of this milestone

I  achievement; historic sign refreshment; historic tree maintenance; City tree survey;
  preservation of historic properties; Senate Bill (SB) 9 implications for historic
  properties; requirements for consistency in design for remodeling and accessory
  dwelling units; steps for Phase 2 of this project; Mills Act agreement details; SB 10
  exemptions for designated historic districts; Secretary of the Interior standards as
  the basis for reviewing for historic properties; kudos for the report; and the report
  as a facilitation for collaboration with property owners.

  A motion was made by Council Member Ding, seconded by Council Member
  Menchaca, to adopt Resolution No. 23-63 approving the Citywide Historic
  Resources Survey Report.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  CHAN, DING, MENCHACA, WU, HARRINGTON
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN :  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

I  C. COMMUNITY SPECIAL EVENTS 2023-24

  Community Services Director Perez made the presentation .

  Clarifying discussion included budget impacts from  prior and  potential
  collaboration with outside groups.

  The following provided comments or spoke in opposition to a fireworks event and
  proposed alternatives. Mary Garcia, resident; Viki Goto, resident and Human Equity,

  CITY COUNC IL REGULAR MEETING MIN UTES  Pag e 4 of 6  October 3, 2023
   Access and Relations (HEAR) Commission Vice-Chair; Chasity Jennings-Nunez,
  resident; and Sonia Lyn, resident.

  Andrew, resident, questioned details of a proposed Memorial Day Veteran's
  Coalition event sponsorship.

  Discussion included appreciation for staff's realistic pricing of potential events;
  historical cost versus budget for those events; budget figures do not include
  staffing costs; historical sponsorship of events, benefits for sponsors and timeline

I  for soliciting sponsorships; desire for a two-day Lunar New Year event; staff
  th
  workload for potential fundraising; and desire for a drone show for the 4 of July
  to set the City apart from surrounding cities.

  Following discussion on specific events there was a consensus of the City Council
  for events as follows:

  •  One or two-day Lantern Festival on Feb 16-17, 2024.

  •  Memorial Day/Veteran's Day - flags display with funding from non-
  departmental budget; possible collaboration with the Veterans Coalition.

  •  Walk to LA - possible coordination with the City's birthday; encourage City of
  Los Angeles to reinitiate.

  •  City Birthday Celebration - partner with Historical Association or other groups;
  staff to return to Council with proposal.

  •  4th of July- event to be held on July 4th ; no fireworks; not to be held at Vincent

I  Lugo Park or McKinley school; continue with the parade with enhancements for
  one more year while staff looks into alternatives; staff to get quotes for drone
  and laser light shows.

  •  Mid-Autumn Moon Festival - keep the lunch for seniors, as is.

  •  Wellness Expo - add budget, bring proposal with mid -year budget, solicit ideas
  from the HEAR Commission.

  •  Holiday Tree Lighting - needs to be changed with more food and family-
  oriented activities.

  •  Mission to Mission (Active SGV) - desire to continue participation, perhaps
  combined with an environmental event.

  8. PUBLIC COMMENT - None.

  9. CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

I  Public Works Director/City Engineer de Vinck announced 411 with the Chief on every
  second Tuesday from 6:00 - 7:00 P.M . in the Council Chamber, and that the Federal
  Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) would be conducting a National Test on
  October 4, 2023, at 11 :20 A.M .

  10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Vice Mayor Wu reported on his attendance at a Historical Association dinner, reported
  that the U.S. Chinese Women Association and YWCA teamed up with the Community

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 5 of 6  October 3, 2023
   Services Department to provide a luncheon for San Gabriel senior citizens; reported
  on his attendance at the 52 nd Anniversary Celebration Gala of the Chinatown Service
  Center, which donated live translation service via iPads to the San Gabriel Police
  Department last year; and reported on his attendance at the 2nd Mental Health Expo;
  thanked the HEAR Commission for their work on the event; and thanked the City of
  Hope for their donation which made multi-lingual translation possible.

  Council Member Chan reported on his attendance at the League of California Cities
  conference.

I  Council Member Menchaca reported on the Coffee with a Cop event held at Blossom
  Market; congratulated Public Information Officer Clara Tsang and Team for the
  multilingual Discover publication; announced a press conference at La Casa where
  Assemblymember Mike Fong will present a $35,000 check to help with infrastructure;
  reported on her attendance at a local playhouse and commented on its financial
  support structure and her desire for similar support for the Mission Playhouse.

  Council Member Ding commented on the Historical Association dinner and Mid-
  Autumn Festival senior meals at the Grapevine, thanked the Chinese Service Center for
  their service to the community; stated he had enjoyed the Mental Health Expo;
  announced an upcoming Asia Fall Festival at Santa An ita Race Park and a student
  speech contest on October 14, 2023, sponsored by the San Gabriel Lions Club; and
  reported that Ningbo, China, has interest in being a Sister or Friendship City with San
  Gabriel.

  11. CLOSED SESSION

I
  A. CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL - ANTICIPATED  LITIGATION
  (GOVERNMENT CODE §54956.9 [d] [2]) (One Case)

  There was no reportable action.

  12. ADJOURNMENT

  The meeting was adjourned at 10:43 P.M. in memory of Senator Dianne Feinstein.
